chapter: Dance jobs and the opera house
title: Paul Moyer and the clarinet player who took his horn apart
summary: Dejan sorts out the Moyers: old man Moyer's son took his clarinet apart piece by piece while playing; Paul played drums and Oynice was the clarinetist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: As you were saying, it's good to catch up on a few of these little things that we might forget later. Who was the fellow that you told us about that took the clarinet apart and ended up playing on the mouthpiece?
Paul Moyer. Paul was a drummer, huh? He was a fellow that played with Paul Moyer. No, played with an old man Moyer. That's his son I'm talking about. Paul was a drummer.
What was his son's name? He wanted to play the clarinet.

I used to go play with him and they had a trumpet player by the name of La Quasi very often. Oh, was Paul Moyer's son that took the- Old man Paul Moyer. Not this Paul Moyer that died sometime ago. That's the one who used to take the clarinet apart and play all apart. That's the one that took it apart.

He used to lay on the floor lay on the bench and take one piece at a time and put it down and take the other piece and put it down and take the other piece and just go and play until he get to the mouthpiece. He was just enjoying that. Oh, he just enjoyed that. Yeah, I learned a lot of foolishness from him. Yeah. And Paul was playing drum then. He was a little bit of kid playing drum with his dad in the band.

If he was playing drum. I said Paul Moyer played drum, but Oynice Moyer was the clarinet. Oynice. Oynice, Paul Moyer's brother. Yeah, because when I first went to the opera house, that's who I went to the opera house with, you know. With Paul Moyer playing drum and Sammy Hopkins playing piano.
